name: HardenedBSD
summary: A security-hardened downstream fork of FreeBSD implementing comprehensive defense-in-depth exploit mitigations, including mandatory ASLR, SafeStack, Clang Control Flow Integrity (CFI), SEGVGUARD, and PaX-inspired memory protections across the base system and ports.

content.introduction: HardenedBSD is an open-source security-hardened operating system founded in 2014 by Shawn Webb and Oliver Pinter. Originating as a security-focused downstream fork of FreeBSD, HardenedBSD enhances the complete FreeBSD kernel, base system, and ports collection with advanced exploit mitigation technologies inspired by PaX and modern compiler sanitizers, providing a robust defense-in-depth computing foundation.
content.what_is_it: HardenedBSD is a production-oriented operating system that delivers a fully functional FreeBSD environment while strictly enforcing compiler-level and kernel-level mitigations against memory corruption attacks. By combining FreeBSD's advanced features—such as OpenZFS, Jails, and bhyve—with mandatory Address Space Layout Randomization (ASLR), SafeStack, and Control Flow Integrity (CFI), HardenedBSD neutralizes entire vulnerability classes without requiring application-level code rewrites.
content.origin_and_freebsd_relationship: Founded in 2014, HardenedBSD began with the goal of bringing PaX-style exploit mitigation technologies from Linux/Grsecurity into the FreeBSD kernel. While FreeBSD prioritizes maximum out-of-the-box backward binary compatibility and peak performance, HardenedBSD prioritizes system defense and memory safety. The project maintains rigorous upstream tracking, migrating its primary package build infrastructure to 15-STABLE in December 2025 alongside development branches tracking 16-CURRENT.
content.memory_protections_and_compiler_hardenin: HardenedBSD applies deep, proactive exploit mitigations derived from the PaX project and modern computer security research. By default, the operating system enforces full Address Space Layout Randomization (ASLR), randomizing mmap base addresses, main executable mappings (PIE), the stack, and memory allocators across all user-space processes. It integrates SafeStack (part of LLVM's Clang toolchain), which splits the traditional call stack into a safe stack for control flow pointers and an unsafe stack for local buffers and arrays, effectively mitigating stack-based buffer overflows and Return-Oriented Programming (ROP) exploitation. Furthermore, HardenedBSD enforces strict W^X (Write XOR Execute) memory protections, preventing malicious execution of dynamic code in writable memory segments. The project actively evaluates Forward-Edge Control Flow Integrity (CFI) to validate function pointer targets during runtime.
content.kernel_defenses_and_segvguard: At the kernel level, HardenedBSD incorporates SEGVGUARD, a specialized rate-limiting defense mechanism that detects repeated segmentation faults and memory aborts generated by a specific binary or user account. When automated brute-force attacks attempt to guess randomized memory offsets or defeat ASLR entropy, SEGVGUARD suspends or blocks the affected binary from executing for an administratively configured duration. The kernel also randomizes process identifiers (PIDs), restricts information leakage via `/proc` and `linprocfs`, hardens sysctl interfaces, and implements non-executable kernel memory mappings to protect sensitive supervisor data structures from unauthorized user-space inspection.
content.maintenance_status_and_infrastructure: HardenedBSD is maintained by an independent security engineering team that actively tracks upstream FreeBSD CURRENT and STABLE source branches. The project maintains its own Git repositories containing security patchsets, custom Clang compiler modifications, and hardened base system configurations. It operates an automated package building farm using modified Poudriere builders, producing hundreds of pre-compiled binary packages with SafeStack and PIE enabled by default. While HardenedBSD contributes security enhancements and bug reports back to the FreeBSD Project, it operates independently, catering specifically to security researchers, defense-in-depth infrastructure, and high-threat production workloads.
content.package_repositories_and_pkg_toolchain:
Binary packages are handled by `pkg`, whose bootstrap program the base system builds from `usr.sbin/pkg` (`pkg.c`, `rsa.c`, `dns_utils.c`, `config.c`, `ecc.c`, `hash.c`) and installs together with the repository definitions placed in `/etc/pkg`. The `Makefile` lists the four repository files in `CONFS` (`HardenedBSD.conf`, `HardenedBSD.pkgbase.conf`, `HardenedBSD.pkgbase.tor.conf` and `HardenedBSD.tor.conf`), sets `CONFSDIR` to `/etc/pkg` with `CONFSMODE` 644 and defines `PKGCONF?=HardenedBSD.conf`.

The default repository, named `HardenedBSD`, points to `https://pkg.hardenedbsd.org/HardenedBSD/pkg/${ABI}` with `mirror_type` set to `none`, `signature_type` set to `fingerprints` and fingerprints read from `/usr/share/keys/pkg`. The Tor variant uses the project onion address with the same `${ABI}` path and ships disabled, as does the pkgbase repository at `https://pkgbase.hardenedbsd.org/pkgbase/HardenedBSD/${ABI}`; the August-September 2026 status report records an explicit change in `bsdinstall` to dissuade pkgbase use. A repository is disabled without editing the shipped file, by creating `/usr/local/etc/pkg/repos/HardenedBSD.conf` with the line `HardenedBSD: { enabled: no }`.

Packages are built on two dedicated hosts named on the infrastructure page: `hbsd-pkg-15-stable-01`, presented as the 15-STABLE/amd64 package builder, and `hbsd-pkg-current-01`, presented as the 16-CURRENT/amd64 package builder. Both answer with a Poudriere web interface.
content.installer_images_and_hardening_controls: HardenedBSD publishes signed installer images. The project README documents fetching the compressed memstick image for the 15-STABLE branch from installers.hardenedbsd.org, together with its signature, and verifying it with `ssk-keygen -Y verify` against a published SSH public key; SSH keys were chosen so that build artifacts can be validated with tools already present in the base system. The build path documented in the README is amd64. The same document lists hardening that extends to third-party software — SafeStack, non-cross-DSO control-flow integrity and retpoline applied to ports as well as base — and states that individual features can be toggled per application and per jail with `secadm` or `hbsdcontrol`, and that the source tree synchronises with FreeBSD every six hours.
content.build_artifacts_mirrors_and_rsync:
Beyond the package repositories, the project publishes and mirrors build artifacts separately. The `installers.hardenedbsd.org/pub` tree exposes the branches `13-stable`, `14-stable`, `15-stable` and `current`, plus `keys`, `cross-dso-cfi` and `pledge` directories; `current/amd64/` contains a further `amd64` subdirectory, and the `keys` and `pledge` entries show modification dates of 1 January 2026 and 14 June 2026.

The mirrors page documents full-tree replication with `rsync -rlv rsync://rsync.hardenedbsd.org/all` toward the local `pub` directory, and lists four official installer-media mirrors: dotsrc in Denmark, Lavabit in Dallas, LAYLO in the Netherlands and Stygian in Montreal, plus a Tor Onion Service mirror at `http://zqsjg25lnx7zratmne3dhbcqt5paehitom3qp2rjmwttuy7gzbzqwayd.onion/pub/hardenedbsd`. The infrastructure page adds that the site and the installation media are themselves reachable through onion endpoints, next to the Radicle node for source and the two package builders.
advantages: Rigorous defense-in-depth exploit mitigations enabled universally by default (ASLR, PIE, SafeStack, CFI)
SEGVGUARD protection halting automated memory corruption and ASLR brute-forcing attacks
Full access to FreeBSD's enterprise features including native OpenZFS, Jails, and bhyve virtualization
Per-binary fine-tuning of hardening parameters via the secadm access control framework
Transparent engineering with frequent public status reports and quarterly release maintenance
disadvantages: Certain complex third-party software packages require mitigation exceptions or custom port patches
Small development team reliant on key individual maintainers compared to larger community OSes
Hardware architecture focus primarily centered on amd64, with arm64 remaining experimental
who_is_it_for: Security engineers and infrastructure architects managing internet-exposed bastions, VPNs, and firewalls
Organizations operating critical FreeBSD services requiring proactive defense against zero-day memory exploits
Researchers studying production compiler sanitizers, Control Flow Integrity, and OS hardening
who_is_it_not_for: Administrators who require 100% turnkey binary drop-in package compatibility for unmaintained proprietary binaries
General home desktop users looking for casual gaming and rapid bleeding-edge consumer driver updates
content.verdict: HardenedBSD is a FreeBSD-derived operating system focused on exploit mitigations. It enforces ASLR, SafeStack, Clang CFI, and SEGVGUARD while retaining OpenZFS and Jails, adding defenses against memory corruption attacks.
